mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: New Zealand Companies Office (Registrar of Companies)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path (default for all Apostille Convention receiving states): (1) Certified true copy issued by the Registrar; (2) Notarization by a New Zealand Notary Public; (3) Apostille issued by MFAT Authentication Unit. For non-member states only: (1) Notarization; (2) MFAT legalization; (3) Consular legalization by the receiving state's embassy or consulate in New Zealand. These two paths are mutually exclusive and must never be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certificate of Compliance)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: (1) Print certified copy from Companies Office; (2) Notarization by NZ Notary Public; (3) Apostille by MFAT. Parallel consular path for non-member states is never chained with Apostille.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney for Post-Incorporation Banking and Contracting
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: (1) Execute original resolution; (2) Notarization of director signatures; (3) Apostille by MFAT. Non-member state consular path replaces step 3 with MFAT legalization and embassy consular certification; mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (Constitution) certified true copy
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: (1) Certified copy by the company secretary; (2) Notarization; (3) Apostille by MFAT. Consular legalization parallel path only for non-member states; both paths never coexist.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: New Zealand commercial bank (e.g., ANZ, BNZ, ASB, Westpac)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: (1) Original letter on bank letterhead; (2) Notarization of bank officer's signature; (3) Apostille by MFAT. Consular legalization for non-member states is separate; never chain apostille with consular legalization.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All proposed UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories must undergo real-time and periodic screening against the New Zealand Police Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) Suspicious Transaction Screening, the US OFAC SDN list, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU restrictive measures, and the New Zealand Sanctions Act 2018 administered lists. Enhanced due diligence includes adverse media checks, source of wealth verification, politically exposed person (PEP) status detection (including current-term and former-term officeholders and their family members), and a mandatory 48-hour name-screening reboot prior to any account activation or funding. All screening results must be logged in a tamper-evident audit trail preserved for at least seven years under s 48 AML/CFT Act 2009. Any match triggers a frozen onboarding status and immediate submission of a suspicious transaction report to NZ FIU, plus a moratorium on any transactional flow until a full clearance opinion is issued by independent AML compliance counsel.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office - Company Name Reservation Portal (companiesoffice.govt.nz)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names may be in English or Te Reo Maori. All non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into the Latin alphabet using an approved phonetic system. The Companies Office applies a four-tier distinctiveness hierarchy: identical, too similar, deceptively similar, and distinct. No Te Reo transliteration is mandatory for ordinary trading names, but a Te Reo-only name requires an English-language equivalent for public notice purposes unless ministerial consent is obtained.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Companies Office rejects a name reservation, the applicant may appeal within 20 working days by filing a written objection with the Registrar of Companies under s 25(2) of the Companies Act 1993, supporting the application with evidence of distinctiveness and a statutory declaration that the proposed name does not create confusion with an existing registered name. The Registrar may issue a written decision, and an adverse decision may be further appealed to the High Court of New Zealand under s 370. A successful applicant may reapply for a fresh 20-working-day reservation after final appeal; no automatic extension exists, but a new reservation can be made if the original priority period has lapsed.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: In New Zealand, a virtual office or commercial mailbox is permissible for statutory registration, but the Inland Revenue Department (IRD) and the major trading banks (ANZ, ASB, BNZ, Westpac) generally reject virtual-only addresses for an affiliate media buying entity, especially one with high transaction velocity and a Medium-Risk enhanced AML profile. To satisfy commercial substance requirements, the company must maintain a physical operation address (lease or sublease) with a staffed presence, local bank statement mail delivery, and access to accounting records. If a virtual office is used, a private mailbox service with monthly mail forwarding and scanning is tolerated only for non-banking ancillary correspondence, but IRD will challenge tax residency indicators where no physical place of business exists.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Unannounced onsite inspections by the New Zealand Companies Office are rare, but the IRD and the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE) conduct compliance visits for suspected shell operations. Checkpoints for inspection triggers: (i) registered office corresponds only to a virtual mailbox; (ii) no operational website or physical signage; (iii) annual return lists a UBO with no address in New Zealand; (iv) banking transactions flow to high-risk jurisdictions without commercial justification; (v) the company claims zero employees but files high gross advertising revenue. Quantified risk: approximately 30% annual probability of an IRD/MBIE substance audit for a newly incorporated affiliate media company using a virtual address, rising to 70% if the company also lacks an in-country director or local accountant.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand), Part 2, sections 10 to 19 (incorporation), section 39 (consideration for share subscriptions), sections 41 to 43 (allotment of shares and share register), sections 187 and 188 (registered office and address for service), and sections 126 to 131 (general powers of directors)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), Wellington, New Zealand
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of a Company (digital application filed through the New Zealand Companies Office website) leading to the issuance of a New Zealand Certificate of Incorporation and New Zealand Business Number (NZBN)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. New Zealand law imposes no minimum paid-up capital and no blocked escrow account requirement for a limited company. Shares may be issued at no par value and for such consideration as the directors determine, which may be zero if the constitutional documents and Companies Act 1993 permit.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [SUBJECT COMPANY] LIMITED

AT A MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [SUBJECT COMPANY] LIMITED (the Company), duly convened and held at the registered office of the Company on [date], 2025, at [time], the Chairperson confirmed that a quorum was present. The following resolutions were proposed, seconded, and passed unanimously:

1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION. THAT the allotment and issue of [number] ordinary shares of no par value in the share capital of the Company to the subscribers named in the application for incorporation be and is hereby ratified and approved. The directors are authorized to execute and deliver subscriber share subscription agreements, determine the consideration payable, including, if applicable, no initial consideration, receive such consideration in cash or as otherwise lawfully permitted, and enter the allotment in the Company's share register in accordance with the Companies Act 1993 and the Company's constitution.

2. ADOPTION OF REGISTERED OFFICE. THAT the registered office of the Company be and is hereby fixed and adopted at the address set out in the application for incorporation, namely [registered office address, New Zealand], and the directors are authorized to open, equip, and maintain the registered office, to lodge notices of registered office and address for service with the New Zealand Companies Office, and to keep all statutory registers at that office as required by law.

3. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. THAT [name of bank], or any other bank determined by the directors, be and is hereby appointed as the principal banker of the Company, and the opening of corporate accounts in the Company's name is authorized. All cheques, deposit forms, wire transfer instructions, automated clearing house instructions, electronic banking transmissions, loan documents, and other banking mandates shall be signed by two directors jointly or by one director together with the company secretary, unless otherwise authorized by subsequent resolution of the board.

4. APPOINTMENT OF STATUTORY OFFICERS. THAT the individuals identified in the application for incorporation be and are hereby appointed as the first directors of the Company, to hold office until removal, resignation, retirement, or disqualification under the Companies Act 1993. THAT [name] be and is hereby appointed Company Secretary to maintain the statutory registers, file annual returns, and attend to compliance matters with the New Zealand Companies Office and Inland Revenue. The directors and company secretary shall have all powers necessary to execute incorporation filings, banking documents, and commercial agreements.

5. GENERAL AUTHORIZATION. THAT any director or the company secretary be and is hereby authorized to sign, execute, deliver, file, and post all requisite forms, instruments, contracts, consents, applications, and notices, and to take all such actions as may be necessary or incidental to give full effect to the foregoing resolutions. The Chairperson declared the resolutions carried unanimously, and the meeting was adjourned.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Availability Search, Director Consent, and Constitutional Preparation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (NZCO), Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE) via www.companiesoffice.govt.nz
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a company name availability search on the New Zealand Companies Office public register. Confirm that the proposed legal name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name and that it does not contain prohibited words. Obtain signed consent to act as director from each proposed director and verify that at least one director resides in New Zealand or Australia, or is a director of a company registered in New Zealand, as required under the Companies Act 1993. If the Company does not adopt a custom constitution, the default constitution set out in Schedule 2 of the Companies Act 1993 will apply. Prepare the registered office address and address for service with the consent of the registered office provider. Use the RealMe portal or online authentication of each subscriber before submitting the company application.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name and up to three alternative names
Statutory declaration or written consent to act as director for each proposed director
Personal identification and residential address details for directors and shareholders
Registered office address and identical address for service with landlord or service provider consent
Proposed constitution, if any, or confirmation that the default constitution will apply
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name reservation is rejected or placed on query, use the Companies Office name availability search to select an alternative available name and resubmit the consent forms and application. If director consent is deficient, obtain a corrected signed consent and re-upload through the online portal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Application for Incorporation and Issuance of Certificate and NZBN
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (NZCO), Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE) via www.companiesoffice.govt.nz
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the New Zealand Companies Office online platform and complete the Application for Registration of a Company under the Companies Act 1993. Enter the exact company name, registered office address, address for service, director details, shareholder details, share structure, and principal business purpose. In the business classification field, select the applicable industry classification consistent with ISIC 7310, namely digital advertising, marketing, affiliate media buying, and lead generation services. Confirm that the constitution, if any, is uploaded and that each director and shareholder has consented to their appointment and shareholding. Pay the non-refundable government registration fee using an acceptable payment method. Upon successful validation, the Registrar will issue the Certificate of Incorporation and New Zealand Business Number, which together confirm the legal existence and registration of the Company.
required_dossiers: Electronic application for registration duly completed and signed
Certificate or consent of director appointments
Constitution, if adopted, plus notice explaining any deviations from default rules
Registered office and address for service details
Government filing fee payment confirmation
Identification documents for beneficial owners and directors as required by the Registrar
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Office issues a query or suspends the application, respond within the stated statutory timeframe, usually 20 working days, through the online portal by correcting any inconsistency in director details, registered office consent, or share capital particulars. If the fee was declined, resubmit the payment. Once the defect is cured, the application is processed and the certificate is issued retroactively where lawfully permitted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registrations with Inland Revenue for Income Tax, GST, and Employer Obligations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD), Te Tari Taake, New Zealand
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, use the New Zealand Business Number and Certificate of Incorporation to register the Company with Inland Revenue for income tax purposes through MyIR. Obtain an IRD number for the Company. Assess the requirement to register for goods and services tax where annual taxable supplies exceed or are expected to exceed NZD 60,000 in any 12-month period; voluntary registration is also available. If the Company will employ workers, register as an employer for PAYE, KiwiSaver, and accident compensation levies as applicable. Provide details of the main business activity, estimated turnover, and expected source of income from affiliate media buying and digital advertising services. The registration can be completed entirely online using the RealMe or MyIR credentials of the authorized director or tax agent.
required_dossiers: New Zealand Certificate of Incorporation
New Zealand Business Number confirmation
IRD numbers for directors and resident shareholders, where available
Actual or projected New Zealand and offshore taxable turnover for GST threshold assessment
Bank account details for any tax refunds
Employment structure details if PAYE, KiwiSaver, or ACC registration is required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the IRD registration is queried, provide the requested information through MyIR, including full entity ownership details and turnover projections. If a GST registration is challenged due to projected turnover, submit a revised forecast and supporting evidence of advertising revenue. Correct any inconsistencies within 28 days to avoid late filing penalties.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Bank Account Opening, AML/KYC Verification, and Payment Rail Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered New Zealand bank, non-bank deposit taker, or approved financial institution; subject to supervision under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 by the Financial Markets Authority and the Department of Internal Affairs
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate business bank account in the name of the Company with a New Zealand registered bank or a recognized non-bank financial institution approved for corporate clients. Undergo customer due diligence and beneficial ownership verification as required by the AML/CFT Act 2009. Provide the bank with a certified copy of the Certificate of Incorporation, the constitution, and the board resolution authorizing account opening and mandated signatories. Submit personal identification and proof of residential address for directors, shareholders, and any beneficial owners holding more than 25 percent of the Company. Provide a short business profile describing affiliate media buying, principal counterparties, expected transaction volumes, source of funds, and target payment rails, including Mercury ACH, wire transfer, and Wise. After internal AML/KYC approval, execute the banking mandate and activate the requested payment channels.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and NZBN
Constitution and board resolution authorizing account opening
Certified passport or national identity card for all directors, signatories, and beneficial owners
Proof of residential address not older than three months for all beneficial owners
Beneficial ownership and source of funds declaration
Business plan covering ISIC 7310 digital advertising activities and projected overseas or domestic payment flows
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank declines or counsels the account application, request a written adverse decision, supply supplementary beneficial ownership or source-of-funds documentation, or approach another registered financial institution. If the AML/CFT query is based on jurisdiction or industry-risk concerns, provide contractual evidence of legitimate affiliate advertising arrangements and third-party due diligence reports.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Ongoing Statutory Compliance, Annual Return, and Tax Filing Maintenance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (NZCO) and Inland Revenue Department (IRD)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, maintain the statutory registers for shareholders, directors, and persons who have ceased to be directors, together with minute books and accounting records. File the annual return with the New Zealand Companies Office each year on the Company's filing date and pay the applicable annual return fee. Prepare financial statements if required by law, considering exemptions for small companies under the Financial Reporting Act 2013; if exempt, retain adequate accounting records to support tax returns. File income tax returns with Inland Revenue each financial year, file GST returns at the appropriate frequency, and file any PAYE, KiwiSaver, and ACC returns if the Company employs staff. Retain all board resolutions, share allotment records, and contracts related to affiliate media buying to demonstrate the commercial substance and compliance with disclosure obligations.
required_dossiers: Company formation documents and constitution
Share register, director register, and minute book
Annual return filing payment record
Financial statements or accounting records sufficient to complete tax returns
GST and income tax working papers
Employment and payroll records if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the annual return is rejected or late, file the return immediately through the Companies Office portal and pay any late fee. For tax default, file the omitted return and make voluntary disclosure to Inland Revenue to reduce penalties. If a registrar queries an early change in directors or officeholders, submit the prescribed notice of change within the statutory period.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) of New Zealand, electronic portal: myIR (https://www.ird.govt.nz)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident entity must apply for an IRD number (tax file number) by completing the Non-Resident Company IRD Number Application form (IR742) and submitting it to Inland Revenue. The application requires certified copies of the entity's incorporation documents, proof of foreign tax residence, and details of the New Zealand registered office or agent. The IRD number is issued within 10-15 working days and serves as the GST registration number if the entity registers for GST.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None (New Zealand does not have check-the-box elections; however, hybrid mismatch rules under the Taxation (Neutralising Base Erosion and Profit Shifting) Act 2018 may apply to cross-border arrangements)

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 (mandatory registration if taxable supplies exceed this threshold in a 12-month period; voluntary registration allowed)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping mandate. GST-registered businesses must issue tax invoices (standard or simplified) containing prescribed details, and retain records for 7 years. Inland Revenue accepts electronic invoices (e-invoicing) via the Peppol network, but it is not mandatory. There is no API-based pre-clearance requirement.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to exports of goods (removed from New Zealand within 28 days of supply) and to certain services (e.g., services supplied to non-residents who are outside New Zealand at the time of supply, and the services are not supplied to a person in New Zealand). For digital advertising and media buying services, zero-rating applies if the recipient is a non-resident and the services are not performed in New Zealand, subject to the 'direct export' criteria under Section 11A of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Bill of Entry) lodged via New Zealand Customs Service (Trade Single Window)
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing physical export of goods (if applicable)
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) or bank statement showing foreign exchange receipt from the overseas customer
Contract or purchase order with the non-resident customer
Evidence of the recipient's non-resident status (e.g., overseas tax registration or address)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If zero-rating is claimed without sufficient evidence, Inland Revenue may assess GST at 15% on the supply, impose shortfall penalties of up to 150% of the tax shortfall (depending on whether the error is not deliberate, deliberate, or abusive), and charge use-of-money interest. For fraudulent claims, criminal penalties may apply under the Tax Administration Act 1994, including fines up to NZD 50,000 for individuals and NZD 250,000 for companies, and imprisonment up to 5 years. Retrospective clawback can extend to the original supply date.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Pūtea Matua)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand operates a fully liberalised and freely convertible currency regime under the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act 2021 and the Foreign Exchange Control Regulations. There are no restrictions on current account transactions, capital account movements, or profit remittances. Non-residents may freely transfer NZD and foreign currency, open accounts, and repatriate capital, dividends, and fees without prior central bank approval. The NZD is a free-floating currency, and the Reserve Bank does not mandate any surrender of export proceeds or conversion obligations. However, the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 (AML/CFT Act) imposes reporting and verification duties on financial institutions for cross-border transactions, including prescribed transaction reports for cash and wire transfers over NZD 10,000. Certain capital inflows such as foreign direct investments exceeding NZD 100 million may trigger screening under the Overseas Investment Act 2005, but this does not impose currency exchange restrictions. For the entity described, an affiliate media buying operation conducted via a New Zealand limited company can therefore transact in multiple currencies, hold foreign currency accounts, and remit global advertising payments with minimal exchange control friction, provided standard reporting and AML/CFT obligations are met. The Reserve Bank does not distinguish between onshore and offshore businesses for convertibility purposes, and the medium-risk nature of the sector does not alter the open capital account framework.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory timeline or mandatory conversion ratio for export foreign currency receipts in New Zealand. Exporters are entitled to retain 100% of foreign currency earnings in foreign currency accounts and may convert to NZD at their discretion. The Reserve Bank collects balance-of-payments survey data, and the Tax Administration Act requires transferring money from the overseas to be reportable for tax purposes, but no surrender requirement applies. For affiliate media buying services deemed as cross-border exports of digital services, all proceeds can be kept offshore or onshore as the entity prefers.

Corporate Account with Foreign Exchange Lines
Business Account with Committed FX Facility

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMI providers such as Wise Business and Airwallex are legally permitted to service New Zealand entities under the AML/CFT Act, provided they are registered as financial services providers on the Financial Service Providers Register (FSPR) and licensed by the Financial Markets Authority or the Department of Internal Affairs. In practice, Wise has secured a New Zealand money remittance banking partnership and can offer multi-currency accounts, while Airwallex offers global payment accounts with local receiving details. However, tier-1 domestic commercial banks remain the preferred route for the capital escrow and operational treasury due to robust correspondent banking networks and direct SWIFT membership. An EMI cannot replace a licensed New Zealand registered bank for statutory purposes such as capital verification under a capital injection plan or when serving as a party to a bank guarantee. For a medium-risk affiliate media buying entity, an EMI is highly viable as a secondary settlement rail for small-value cross-border affiliate payouts, but the core corporate banking relationship must be with a domestic tier-1 bank to maintain creditability with ad platform partners and tax authorities. Legal constraints: EMIs cannot issue credit facilities and may impose subaccount operation restrictions; a New Zealand entity must still appoint a local agent or compliance officer to meet the FSPR obligations if the EMI is treated as an overseas service provider.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical appearance in a branch is not an absolute statutory requirement under New Zealand AML/CFT law, which permits electronic identity verification and remote client onboarding under the Department of Internal Affairs guidelines. However, for a medium-risk enhanced-scrutiny affiliate media buying entity, the majority of tier-1 domestic banks apply a risk-based approach: statutory directors may complete onboarding via video conference with verified identity documents, but they must provide a local registered office address and a compliance contact in New Zealand. If the beneficial owner resides in a high-risk jurisdiction or if the bank is not entitled to rely on electronic KYC (eKYC) for foreign citizens, a consular proxy opening may be permitted only with an apostilled and legalised certification of identity and source of funds; most banks still require at least one director or the authorised signatory to be physically present at the final interview. We therefore mandate planning for a physical or consular-completed KYC interview within 30 days of incorporation to accelerate account approval.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained high-volume inbound deposits exceeding NZD 1 million per month from foreign ad networks with opaque settlement cascades
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide audited financial statements and platform payout reports from programmatic ad exchanges (e.g., Google Ads, Meta, and third-party ad servers), identifying merchant ID and settlement ledger; grant the bank portal access to the entity's advertising account showing campaign spend, click-through rates, and monthly reconciliation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership structure with a non-resident trust or corporate nominee obscuring the ultimate founder's identity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit: trust deed and deed of variation (English translation), a chain of title graph with all intermediate entities, Certificate of Incorporation and registered agent confirmation from each offshore jurisdiction, plus a notarised statutory declaration from every beneficial owner disclosing underlying economic interest.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border wire transfers to high-risk sanctioned or embargoed territories for media buying inventory or affiliate payouts
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a comprehensive sanctions compliance program, including SWIFT screening logs, a third-party certification from a sanctions list screening tool (e.g., Dow Jones, LexisNexis), and the affiliate IP address and final device confirmation proving no traffic originates from prohibited regions for existing clients.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The account's destination being a shell entity in a tax-haven jurisdiction with no material marketing operations or digital footprint
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Produce a full-year media buying business plan with committed contracts from at least two independent advertisers, audited audit trail of click data from a third-party click-through and bot fraud detection service, and evidence of a physical commercial lease or co-working agreement in NZ, plus a tax residence certificate from IRD showing New Zealand economic substance.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For inbound capital injection from a non-resident parent or shareholder, use SWIFT MT103 with a purpose code consistent with the IMF Balance of Payments classification — specifically code DI (Direct Investment) or, for non-equity finance, code 611 (Loans for direct investment). The domestic NZ tier-1 bank will require a capital verification letter from a registered New Zealand auditor or chartered accountant when funds exceed NZD 50,000; the letter must confirm the capital is credited to the entity's corporate account and not commingled with revenue. The remitter must include a detailed reference such as 'EQUITY INJECTION - SHAREHOLDER LOAN - NZ_LTD - 2025/26' to match the Companies Office records. All funds are freely convertible to NZD at spot by the receiving bank, or can remain in the original currency in a multi-currency account with no conversion obligation. For visa and reserve bank statistical purposes, the entity must report the inbound transfer in its monthly balance-of-payments return if the value exceeds NZD 1 million.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For payments to international affiliates and advertising platforms, the primary clearing rail is SWIFT MT103 on the bank's correspondent network. The entity may also use Commercial Letters of Credit (LC) for large media purchases exceeding USD 250,000 where the supplier requires bank guarantee settlement, and Documentary Collections (D/P and D/A) for lower-risk media inventory purchases. Since the underlying transaction is digital services rather than physical goods, use purpose code 900 or 222 according to the Business/Financial statement instructions. All outbound wires must be pre-verified against the AML/CFT sanction list; payments above NZD 10,000 need a prescribed transaction report. Domestic NZD payments can be cleared via the High Value Clearing System (HVCS) in real time; cross-border settlement in USD, EUR, or AUD will automatically route via the bank's liquidity pool, and the treasury department should pre-fund a settlement account with multi-currency balances to avoid T+2 conversion friction.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX forward contracts (plain vanilla, maximum 12-month tenor)
FX swaps for temporary cross-currency liquidity alignment
Currency option combinations (zero-premium collars) with a counterparty limit of NZD 5 million
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are available but highly discouraged for NZD since the currency is freely deliverable; the reserve bank does not restrict forward transactions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 12 months of incorporation for the first return; thereafter within 12 months of the date on which the previous annual return was filed, with the anniversary date falling no later than the last day of the month immediately preceding the anniversary of the filing due date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of NZD 100 (approximately USD 60) in addition to the filing fee; continued non-filing for a continuous period of not less than 12 months gives the Registrar power to issue a notice of intention to remove the company from the New Zealand Register, followed by administrative strike-off if no objection is received within the statutory notice period.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a standard 31 March balance date, the IR4 return must be filed by 7 July following the end of the tax year; for an approved non-standard balance date, by the 7th day of the fourth month after the balance date; tax agents may qualify for a later extension date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of NZD 50 per return initially, plus NZD 10 per working day for up to 50 days, bringing the maximum late filing penalty to NZD 500; unpaid tax attracts an immediate 1% late payment penalty, an additional 4% penalty if still unpaid one week later, a further 8% penalty if still unpaid one month later, and use-of-money interest at the prevailing IRD underpayment rate on the outstanding amount until fully paid.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited Financial Statements and Auditor's Report (if large or FMC reporting entity)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, MBIE
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 5 months after balance date if the company is required to file financial statements under the Financial Reporting Act 2013; for a 31 March balance date this ordinarily means filing by 31 August
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance is an offence under the Financial Reporting Act 2013; the company and every director who failed to comply may be liable on conviction to a fine of up to NZD 100,000, and the Registrar may also take action to remove or formally default the entity on the public register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Shareholder and Director Confirmation / Beneficial Ownership Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Contained in and due with the annual return; any share allotment or transfer must be recorded in the Register of Members and notified to the Companies Office on the prescribed form within 20 working days, while anticipated changes in significant beneficial ownership of 25% or more must be reported under the beneficial ownership confirmation protocol within 30 days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain and update the statutory registers and to notify share changes renders the company and its officers liable to infringement fees and court penalties under the Companies Act 1993, and such omissions are also grounds for administrative removal where the annual return is not filed.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A compulsory independent audit by a qualified auditor licensed in New Zealand is mandatory for every FMC reporting entity irrespective of size. For a non-FMC company, a mandatory audit is triggered when the company is 'large' under section 45 of the Financial Reporting Act 2013, being an entity that, in each of the two immediately preceding accounting periods, satisfies at least two of the following quantitative thresholds: (a) total assets exceed NZD 60 million; (b) total revenue exceeds NZD 100 million; (c) 100 or more full-time equivalent employees. A company below these thresholds is normally exempt from statutory audit and from filing audited financial statements unless the shareholders elect otherwise or another enactment imposes an audit obligation.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: New Zealand equivalents to IFRS for Tier 1; New Zealand IFRS Reduced Disclosure Regime for Tier 2; small and medium non-reporting entities preparing general purpose financial statements may adopt the NZ Accounting Standards Framework for for-profit entities, while FMC reporting entities must comply with full NZ IFRS or the applicable approved regime. Financial statements must be expressed in New Zealand dollars unless a different presentation currency is required or permitted by the applicable standard.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand currently uses the annual return as the primary annual corporate confirmation mechanism, containing the registered office, director, shareholder, share structure, and large-company status snapshot. Share transfers and new allotments must be entered in the Register of Members, and an allotment or change notice must be lodged with the Companies Office within 20 working days; where beneficial ownership information is in scope under the enhanced AML/CFT and beneficial ownership confirmation protocol, significant beneficial owners holding 25% or more of voting shares or effective control must be identified on an ongoing basis, confirmed with the annual return, and any change to that beneficial ownership must be reported within 30 days of the transfer event. The company must also preserve internal beneficial ownership and customer due-diligence records for at least 5 years after the relationship ends.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 150 - USD 450 for standard registered office and registered agent service; USD 500 - USD 1,200 for full corporate secretarial maintenance including register maintenance and annual return handling
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 0 for a small exempt entity; USD 8,000 - USD 35,000 for a mandatory statutory audit of a large or FMC reporting affiliate media-buying entity, depending on transaction flow, group complexity, and engagement scope

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: New Zealand does not operate a territorial patent box regime; R&D tax credits are available at 15% for eligible expenditure incurred from the 2021–22 income year, subject to the Research and Development Tax Credit rules. No general free-zone tax holidays exist. The imputation (dividend streaming) regime allows resident shareholders to attach imputation credits, effectively avoiding double taxation, but non-resident shareholders are generally not entitled to imputation credits and face non-resident withholding tax on dividends. Losses may be carried forward indefinitely if shareholder continuity of 49% or more is maintained over the carry-forward period, and loss grouping is available under common ownership.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 Company Income Tax Return filed via myIR (Inland Revenue's electronic filing portal); non-resident companies with a New Zealand source income may instead be required to file an IR4 or an IR3 return depending on the nature of income and presence, but corporate non-residents with a fixed establishment in New Zealand are assessable on New Zealand-source income under the Income Tax Act 2007.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The IR4 must be filed by the 7th day of the month following the balance date (standard balance date 31 March: due 7 July annually); however, if the return is filed by an agent, the extended due date is generally 31 March of the following year for a standard balance date, subject to Inland Revenue's agent extension programme. Final income tax must be paid by the terminal tax date, typically 7 February for a standard 31 March balance date (or 7 April for taxpayers with a tax agent and a non-standard balance date). Provisional tax is payable in three instalments during the year under the standard or GST ratio method.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total income (gross income before expenses), including worldwide income for residents, or New Zealand-source income for non-residents with a New Zealand permanent establishment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident company treated as carrying on business through a fixed establishment in New Zealand, include only assessable income derived from New Zealand sources. Do not include foreign-sourced income unless the company is a New Zealand resident. Attach a schedule reconciling foreign exchange gains and losses arising from cross-border media buying settlements in USD, EUR, or other foreign currencies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total expenses incurred in deriving assessable income, including media inventory costs, affiliate commissions, platform fees, software subscriptions, cloud infrastructure, and staff costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct only expenses that are both incurred in deriving New Zealand-source assessable income and not of a capital nature. For intercompany charges from related overseas entities, strict application of the arm's length standard under transfer pricing rules applies; any excessive or non-arm's length payment to a non-resident associate is non-deductible under sections GC 6 to GC 8 of the Income Tax Act 2007. Apportionment is required where expenses relate to both taxable and non-taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income (Box 1 less Box 2 less allowable deductions and losses carried forward).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a branch or fixed establishment of a non-resident company, New Zealand's domestic rules generally follow the OECD authorised OECD approach (AOA) under the organisation for economic co-operation and development 2010 update: the permanent establishment is deemed to have the capital and profit attributable to it. Adjustments for internal dealings between head office and the New Zealand branch should be reflected, and the return must be prepared on an arm's length attribution basis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Dividends paid, imputation credits attached, and the company's imputation credit account balance.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident company branch is not part of the New Zealand imputation group, but if the entity is a New Zealand resident company, dividend payments to non-resident shareholders trigger non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) under sections RE 12 and RF 8 of the Income Tax Act 2007. Imputation credits cannot generally be attached to dividends paid to non-residents unless the dividend is fully imputed and the shareholder is a New Zealand resident or a resident of a jurisdiction with which New Zealand has a Double Tax Agreement (DTA) that allows imputation credit refunds (rarely). Report all dividends paid and any supplementary dividend paid under the New Zealand-Australia DTA where applicable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses brought forward and offset against current-year net income, subject to shareholder continuity requirements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a New Zealand resident company owned by non-residents, the shareholder continuity requirement under section IA 5 of the Income Tax Act 2007 requires the same persons to hold at least 49% of the voting and market value interests throughout the loss carry-forward period. Media-buying affiliate structures that issue new shares or change beneficial ownership to foreign investors may breach this continuity and forfeit loss utilisation. Losses from foreign-controlled entities must also satisfy the business continuity test if a 49% ownership change occurs.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim for the 15% research and development tax credit on eligible R&D expenditure.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Affiliate media-buying activities generally do not qualify as eligible R&D under section LY 2 of the Income Tax Act 2007 unless software innovation, algorithmic ad-optimisation technology, or machine-learning optimisation is genuinely developed with technical uncertainty and a systematic research plan. Any R&D claim must be accompanied by a supplementary return (IR120) and an R&D supplementary return and, if claimed by a non-resident, must relate to eligible New Zealand core R&D activities performed in New Zealand.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of cross-border related-party transactions, including the volume of intercompany payments and whether transfer pricing documentation has been prepared.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The IR4 requires disclosure of payments to non-resident associates and related-party loan balances. Non-resident media-buying entities must disclose management fees, service fees, platform rebates, or licensing fees paid to foreign affiliates. Inland Revenue's transfer pricing rules treat each related-party transaction as if undertaken between independent persons; failure to furnish sufficient evidence of the arm's length price may lead to recharacterisation and penalties under section ME 47 and the Tax Administration Act 1994.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of an IR4 attracts a late filing penalty of NZ$250 plus an additional NZ$50 per month for every month the return remains outstanding, up to a maximum of NZ$1,000 for small businesses or more for large companies. Late payment of income tax attracts an initial late payment penalty of 1% of the unpaid tax, followed by a further 1% each subsequent month, plus interest on the unpaid provisional and terminal tax at the late payment interest rate (currently around 10.27% per annum as of 2025, updated quarterly). Inaccurate or fraudulent returns may attract a shortfall penalty up to 150% of the resulting tax shortfall for evasion, and criminal prosecution under section 143B of the Tax Administration Act 1994 can result in imprisonment of up to five years for intent to evade tax, plus personal liability on directors under the director penalty regime in section 159.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: NRWT on dividends paid by a New Zealand resident company to a non-resident shareholder is generally 15% under the Income Tax Act 2007, except where the dividend is fully imputed and paid to a resident of a country with a DTA containing a 5% zero-rating provision for wholly-owned subsidiaries (e.g. 5% for Australian non-portfolio dividends; 15% under the OECD DTA). For non-portfolio dividends to DTA countries, the rate is typically 5%; for portfolio dividends under most DTAs, 15%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim DTA relief, the non-resident recipient must complete an Inland Revenue form IR458 (Certificate of Residence / Non-Resident Withholding Tax Rate Declaration) and provide it to the payer before the dividend is paid. The payer must hold a valid certificate of residence from the recipient's tax authority confirming the recipient is fiscally resident in the DTA country and has not merely transited residency for treaty-shopping purposes. The recipient must also satisfy the beneficial ownership requirement under the OECD Model Tax Convention Article 10(2) — the recipient must have the right to the income, be subject to tax on it in the residence jurisdiction, and not act as a conduit for another person. Where the beneficial ownership cannot be substantiated, the payer must deduct NRWT at the full domestic rate, and the recipient must request a refund under the applicable mutual agreement procedure (MAP) or through a New Zealand income tax assessment. Inland Revenue has strict anti-treaty-shopping rules; a nominee or agent holding shares on behalf of another is not entitled to relief. For wholly-owned subsidiaries, the 5% rate requires the recipient company to own at least 10% (or 80% under some treaties) of the voting power in the paying company for a 12-month period ending on the date the dividend is declared.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory NRWT on interest paid to a non-resident is 15%, and on royalties is 15%. Under approved DTA networks, interest is generally exempt or reduced to 10% (e.g. China 10%; Australia 10%; United States 0% under certain conditions before application of the portfolio debt rules), and royalties are generally reduced to 5% or 10% (e.g. Australia 5%; China 10%; United States 5% for film royalties and 10% for others). The payer must apply an approved approved issuer levy (AIL) of 2% on qualifying interest paid to non-resident associated persons if the interest is not subject to NRWT due to the payer's election, but this is not available for royalties. Royalties for the use of or the right to use intellectual property, including software licences, algorithms, media optimisation models, and digital advertising technologies, are sourced in New Zealand to the extent the payment is made by a New Zealand resident or a non-resident's fixed establishment in New Zealand. The approved arm's length royalty rate must be documented through a transfer pricing analysis under the Income Tax Act 2007 section GC 7.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: New Zealand has no statutory de minimis threshold for local documentation, but a taxpayer with cross-border related-party transactions above NZ$10 million in aggregate value must prepare and keep contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation under sections GC 13 and 78 of the Tax Administration Act 1994, consistent with the OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines and the Inland Revenue Transfer Pricing Guidelines (IR1044). For a media-buying affiliate with high-volume intercompany transactions (ad inventory procurement, affiliate commissions, and service fees), the NZ$10 million aggregate threshold will almost always be exceeded; Master File and Local File must be prepared. In addition, as of 1 July 2023, New Zealand has implemented Country-by-Country (CbC) reporting requirements for groups with consolidated group revenue of EUR 750 million (NZD equivalent approximately NZ$1.3 billion), requiring the ultimate parent or surrogate parent entity to file with Inland Revenue.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP: Comparable Uncontrolled Price – preferred for media inventory procurement where comparable third-party ad-network or publisher rates exist.

Resale Price: Applicable to an affiliate media reseller who earns a gross margin from buying and reselling digital advertising inventory; the resale price margin should be compared to uncontrolled resellers' margins.
Cost Plus: Applicable to performance-marketing service providers that incur media-buying and campaign-management costs and charge a mark-up to the overseas principal.

TNMM: Transactional Net Margin Method – most commonly used for affiliate lead-gen entities where the net profit margin on sales, operating costs, or assets is benchmarked against comparable independent media-buying companies.

Profit Split: Applicable where the non-resident principal and the New Zealand limited company jointly own unique intangibles (algorithms, proprietary optimisation models, publisher relationships) and each makes unique contributions to the combined profit.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Although New Zealand does not have EU-style Economic Substance Regulations (ESR), Inland Revenue applies the OECD principal purpose test and permanent establishment attribution rules. For a New Zealand limited company claiming tax residency benefits while its board and management decisions occur offshore, the company's place of effective management is relevant under section YD 2 of the Income Tax Act 2007. A non-resident entity that is centrally managed and controlled from New Zealand is a New Zealand tax resident and is taxable on its worldwide income. Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA), consistent with the OECD's authorised OECD approach, require that the New Zealand limited company that books media-buying income must perform the significant people functions of strategic marketing decisions, contracting, inventory sourcing, and management oversight in New Zealand. If these functions are performed offshore by the parent while the New Zealand entity merely holds invoices, the income is attributable to the offshore head office and the New Zealand entity may be treated as a shell with no economic substance; transfer pricing recharacterisation, withholding taxes, and potential non-resident contractor withholding may apply.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion through contrived related-party media-buying charges (Transfer Pricing Fraud)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The New Zealand limited company purchases digital ad inventory or affiliate leads from a non-resident related party at an inflated price, pays a 15% NRWT-free service fee to an offshore affiliate in a zero-tax jurisdiction, and thereby strips nearly all net profit from New Zealand; the arrangement lacks commercial rationale, involves circular payments, and the non-resident affiliate performs no real functions except to hold bank accounts and issue invoices. The New Zealand company then records a loss or negligible profit, avoiding 28% corporate income tax while economically valuable media-buying activities are performed by New Zealand staff.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Sections GC 6 to GC 8 of the Income Tax Act 2007 permit Inland Revenue to disregard the non-arm's length payments and reallocate the profit to the New Zealand entity. A shortfall penalty under section 141D of the Tax Administration Act 1994 of 150% of the resulting tax shortfall applies for evasion or an abusive tax position. Additionally, the promoter penalty under section 141EB may impose NZ$10,000 to NZ$100,000 on any person who promotes a tax avoidance arrangement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Section 159 of the Tax Administration Act 1994 imposes a director penalty for PAYE and GST debts; failure to pay corporate income tax after Inland Revenue issues a notice of assessment can make the director personally liable for the unpaid tax if the company cannot pay. Under the Companies Act 1993, a director who permits the company to incur obligations while knowing it is insolvent faces a civil penalty of up to NZ$200,000 and disqualification from managing a company for up to five years (section 383). Criminal liability for tax evasion under section 143B of the Tax Administration Act 1994 carries imprisonment of up to five years. Inland Revenue may also pursue a travel ban (lodging a departure prohibition order under section 157 of the Tax Administration Act) preventing a director from leaving New Zealand until tax debts are settled or security is provided.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Sham company / Shell entity lacking economic substance and diversion of business income
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The New Zealand Ltd is nominally a director- and officer-less shelf company that holds a Mercury ACH bank account and pays non-resident contractors through Wise, but has no physical office, no employees, no local management meetings, no substantive contracts with publishers, and no records of core campaign management or media-buying decisions. The overseas parent directly executes media-buying contracts with publishers and simply routes revenue through the New Zealand entity as a banking conduit to avoid the parent jurisdiction's tax and to access New Zealand's DTA network without a real business presence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under section YD 2(2) of the Income Tax Act 2007, the company's place of effective management may be held to be in New Zealand, making the shell company a New Zealand resident; however, if the parent controls the entity from abroad and the New Zealand entity is a sham, Inland Revenue can void the arrangement under section BG 1 of the Income Tax Act 2007 (tax avoidance) and reconstruct the taxable position. The company may also be cross-filed under the Financial Reporting Act 2013 and the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 (AML/CFT): failure to maintain a CDD programme for non-resident beneficial owners attracts a civil penalty of up to NZ$200,000 for the company and NZ$100,000 per officer. Offshore companies using New Zealand as a paper presence may be struck off under the Companies Act 1993 and directors banned.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director who knowingly allows a company to be a shell for tax evasion is personally liable for the company's unpaid tax under section 159 of the Tax Administration Act 1994 (as a director penalty), and if the director signs false financial statements or tax returns, section 143B applies with imprisonment up to five years. The director can also be liable for a civil penalty of up to NZ$500,000 under section 139 of the Companies Act 1993 if the company trades while insolvent. The court may pierce the corporate veil under Section 633 of the Companies Act or common law where the company is used as a mere sham, rendering the director personally liable for the full tax shortfall plus interest. Departure prohibition orders under section 157 may be issued against the director for non-payment, and the director's name is placed on the publicly searchable Securities Register and the Director Banning Register.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML/CFT non-compliance and unlicensed financial services in affiliate media remittances
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The affiliate media-buying company acts as a payment intermediary, receiving large volumes of media-buying commissions from international ad networks into its Mercury ACH / Wise accounts and immediately disbursing most funds to foreign beneficiaries (lead-gen affiliates, influencers, and contract publishers) without verifying their beneficial ownership, source of funds, or sanctions status. The entity does not adopt a risk-based AML/CFT programme, does not appoint a compliance officer, does not conduct customer due diligence on high-risk non-resident payees, and processes more than 50 wire transfers per month exceeding NZ$10,000 each, effectively providing remittance services without a Money Service Business licence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: If the company provides financial services through ongoing wire transfers and foreign-exchange settlement, it may be treated as a 'financial institution' under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, requiring registration with the Department of Internal Affairs and compliance with the Act. Failure to comply is a strict liability offence with a maximum penalty of NZ$2 million for each liability finding; each transaction can constitute a separate offence. Inland Revenue may impose non-resident withholding tax additional penalties for failure to file RWT/NRWT returns, and the Serious Fraud Office can prosecute under the Crimes Act 1961 for obtaining a pecuniary advantage by deception (imprisonment up to seven years).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and senior managers of AML/CFT-reporting entities are personally liable where they were knowingly concerned in the contravention: the Court may impose a pecuniary penalty of up to NZ$200,000 per contravention for individuals. Directors who fail to prevent the company from being used to launder illicit media-buying proceeds may be charged with money laundering under section 243 of the Crimes Act 1961, carrying imprisonment up to seven years. A director may also be disqualified from being a director under section 383 of the Companies Act 1993, and the High Court may make a pecuniary penalty order for up to three times the benefit derived from the offending. Additionally, Inland Revenue can blacklist the director through a departure prohibition order and sue the director for the company's tax debt under director penalty provisions, effectively piercing the corporate veil to collect the unpaid tax from the director's personal assets.
